title: Cross-sector generalization of accident-process role classification in occupational accident narratives
why_read: A narrow applied NLP study on classifying roles in French workplace accident reports, of interest mainly to safety-analytics specialists.
analysis: The paper evaluates whether machine learning models trained to classify sentence roles in construction-industry accident reports (like describing a hazardous condition versus the accident event itself) can transfer to other industries like metallurgy and chemicals without retraining. It finds that fine-tuning the model for the task, rather than just using frozen pretrained language representations, notably improves this cross-domain transfer, reaching about 85-86% balanced accuracy. This is solid applied NLP work but has a narrow audience, mostly occupational safety researchers and those building industrial text-classification pipelines rather than general software engineers.
